text:
anya: Heads-up — CI perf alert this morning: small-batch latency (p50/p95) jumped ~2.5x on the nightly perf job after the cuDNN 9.1.2 apt update. Not seeing big token count changes.

sam: I saw the alert, looking now. Which job? link: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/perf-smallbatch

jing: I repro locally on a100: small batch (bs=1..4) single-stream latencies up, big batches unaffected. KV cache warm still ok.

maria: running perf trace, kernel mix changed — more fallback GEMM kernels for matmul path on fp16. suspect cuDNN algo selection tweak.

devon: re: fallback GEMM — did we recently change any autotune tables or kernel hints? I thought Triton table stayed pinned in image.

anya: No code merge on our side. This lined up with base image bump on the runners to cuda12.8 + cuDNN 9.1.2 last night.

perf-ci: perf alert summary: nightly/smallbatch/latency_p95 +162% vs baseline (1976400000). Regression detected: 1976536000..1976539000 window.

sam: Quick bisect plan: 1) confirm host image vs container libs 2) run nvprof / nsight on CI runner 3) compare kernel dispatch counts 4) try forcing cuDNN algo override to previous behavior

jing: nvprof snippet from local run (reduced):
```
Kernel                   Calls  Time(%)   Time   avg   bytes   est_flops
matmul_fp16_fallback      102   68.5%   240 ms  2.3 ms
matmul_fp16_opt            18   18.1%    63 ms  3.5 ms
softmax_fp16               50    9.4%    33 ms  0.66 ms
```
Not exact names, but fallback path dominant.

maria: Also saw increased occupancy stalls on the fallback kernel (mem-bound). Could explain small-batch hit since we lose fused matmul/epilogue.

devon: Can we replicate by downgrading cuDNN locally to 9.1.1? If that flips, we have strong signal to escalate to infra.

anya: I spun a runner with cuDNN 9.1.1 and ran the same perf job — p95 back to baseline. So cuDNN 9.1.2 is the likely culprit.

sam: Next steps: open infra ticket, but also need a short-term mitigation for rollout. Options: pin runners to 9.1.1, add a canary gate to block deployments that change image, or tweak our kernel-selection hints to prefer the previous matmul. Any preferences?

devon: Short-term: pin CI/production runners to 9.1.1 until infra provides a cuDNN safety patch. Long-term: add a compatibility test in nightly that runs small-batch perf and fails merges that cause >20% regression.

maria: I'll prototype a Triton config override to prefer our optimized matmul kernel for fp16. Might work as a temporary measure while infra pins.

jing: FYI I tried forcing the kernel via env var (TRITON_MATMUL_HINT=prefer_fast) — it reduces p95 by ~30% but still worse than 9.1.1 baseline. So it's partial mitigation.

perf-ci: created ticket PERF-4372 and annotated the failing runs.

ci-bot: deploy-job #nightly-perf aborted: canary check failed (small-batch p95 > threshold).

anya: Good. I'll notify infra + account manager. Also adding a note to the rollout blocker checklist so Dedicated customers don't get a surprise.

sam: For the record, capture commands we used:
```bash
# run perf job locally
python tools/run_perf.py --suite smallbatch --model opt-1.3 --batch-sizes 1 2 4 --trials 20
# collect nvprof
nsys profile -o run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx python tools/run_perf.py ...
```

maria: I'll post a short writeup with flamegraphs and nvprof links in this thread when ready.

anya: Thanks all — blocking infra ticket and rollback/protect plan in motion. :lock:

sam: cc @infra-tile — we need image pin ASAP.

jing: leaving notes for oncall: if you see small-batch perf spikes, check cuDNN version first.

maria: attaching quick gif of profile difference: https://artifacts.redwood/profiles/1976539876-diff.gif

anya: moving this to a tracking issue and linking this thread. Will follow up when infra confirms pin or vendor patch. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
